newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt prices up with U.S.Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt prices up with U.S.Treasuries.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were mostly higher in late trade, bolstered by a sharp rise in U.S. Treasury prices and improving economic fundamentals in countries such as Argentina and Mexico, sources said.
"The prices are mainly up with the Treasury market," said one emerging market debt trader at a U.S. investment firm.

At 1715 EST/2215 GMT, Argentine pars AR4C23=RR were 5/8 higher at 65-1/4 bid, Brazilian "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were 3/4 firmer at 77-1/2 bid and Mexican par bonds MX625L19=RR were 7/8 stronger at 75-1/2 bid.

In Argentina, sources said comments Thursday by Economy Minister Roque Fernandez that the country's economic growth rate rose grew 9.0 percent in the fourth quarter certainly helped push its Brady debt higher.

"We are getting pretty good fundamental news across the board in the major countries. In Argentina, there is good news about growth and the fiscal numbers for January appear to be coming in pretty strong. In Mexico, there is pretty good news all around," said Tulio Vera, managing director and head of sovereign research at Bear Stearns & Co.
"Generally the momentum Argentina has been extraordinary," said another market source.
Expectations that the remaining votes required for passage of the re-election amendment in Brazil will move forward at a resonable pace was also seen as a positive, Vera said.
Other market sources attributed some of the price gains in Brazil to short-covering.
The exception in the market was Ecuador which faces a national strike on February 5.
"Ecuador was up early in the day but it is now getting crushed," said one emerging market debt trader at around 1600 EST/2100 GMT.

Sources attributed the price drop to mounting opposition against President Abdala Bucaram's economic plan, a reversal in some of the previously announced policy measures and a sharp rise in the inflation rate of 6.4 percent in January compared with 2.4 percent a year ago.
The Ecuadoran government announced late Wednesday that it was watering down austerity measures in the face of popular unrest.
Among the measures announced by Finance Minister Pablo Concha were the suspension of price increases for utilities and raising some part of the minimum wage.

"In Ecuador, what you are seeing is that just six months after Bucaram's election, the honeymoon appears to have come to an end. I think clearly the outlook for the fundamentals have deteriorated," said Vera.
"What has been driving Ecuador this year is the search for yield. But if you look at where the bonds are trading now, all that yield appears to be captured," said another source.
Elsewhere, sources said Bulgarian Brady bonds continued to rebound after falling sharply Wednesday after President Petar Stoyanov warned of a possible default on debt servicing.
"Bulgaria came back a bit down but liquidity is not great and the debt is solely trading on headlines," said one emerging market debt trader.
Nonetheless, Bulgarian IABs BGFLTH11=RR were 1-1/8 firmer at 49-1/4 bid and its discount bonds BGFLTH24A=RR were 1-7/8 stronger at 53-7/8 bid.
